![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14208490/assets/3556e6b8bda17ab8242b8cd7924e1f5ad975efcbc6c5235667d786b2f0908e1d.png)

Train $A$ travels east from station $S$ at a constant velocity of $153\,\text{km/h},$ and train $B$ travels south toward $S.$ The distance between the trains is increasing at a rate of $35\text{ km/h}.$  What is the speed of train $B$ when train $A$ is $51\,\text{km}$ from the station and train $B$ is $68\,\text{km}$ from the station?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14208490/assets/81d16bb54bdecca628d769cd08d02dd327c5483851c2421fb595446c34f8a124.png)

In the diagram,

- $x$ is the distance between the station and train $A,$

- $y$ is the distance between the station and train $B,$

- $z$ is the distance between the two trains.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $y,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ 

We know that $x=51\,\text{km}$ and $y=68\,\text{km}.$ We can find $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {51}^{2}+{68}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {z}^{2} & =7\,225 \\ z & =85\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=153\,\text{km}/\text{h},$

- $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=35\,\text{km}/\text{h}.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute in the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(51)(153)+2(68)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(85)(35) \\ 136\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =5\,950-15\,606 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{9\,656}{136} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-71.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of train $B$ is $71\,\text{km}/\text{h}.$
